solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Little guy beginning to employ fine performer is generous type

parts.note: Ben is a short form of Benjamin, a little version of the name

indicators.note: the beginning of the word employ is its opening letter

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
an actor is a stage performer

explanation.surface: A small man starts work as a fine performer and turns out to be open-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor who gives money or help to others is the very picture of a generous type.

clue.text: Second team player reinstated?

definitions.meaning: to second a proposal is to support it
a defender in football, rugby or hockey positioned behind the forwards
someone reinstated is returned to their former place

explanation.surface: A reserve-side player brought back into the team.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: three separate senses of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: To support, a defensive position in team sports, and returned to where one was: three senses of one word.

clue.text: Senior member of family having any number of anecdotes

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in algebra
ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings about a person

explanation.surface: An old relative with plenty of stories to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is an older member of the family, often called by this pet name.

clue.text: Pacific almost ruined with no end of plastics, an occurrence one must accept

indicators.note: letters that are ruined are wrecked and reassembled in a new order
with no signals that a letter is to be left out of the word almost
the end of the word plastics is its final letter

explanation.surface: An environmental lament: the Pacific nearly wrecked, though free of plastic waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' looks like an instruction to shorten Pacific, but it is fodder: drop the S (the end of 'plastics') from ALMOST and shuffle ALMOT with PACIFIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase for a thing already done and settled, which those affected have no choice but to accept.

clue.text: Island has real criminal being put away

indicators.note: a criminal put away is locked up and gone, so those letters vanish from the word

parts.note: concrete means real or actual, as opposed to abstract
a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: An island harbours a genuine villain who is due to be jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being put away' does double duty in the surface for jailing, but in the parse it removes CON from CONCRETE.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest Greek island, in the eastern Mediterranean, is a straightforward example of an island.

clue.text: Sir losing head over maiden, maybe surprisingly quickly

parts.note: a maiden in cricket is an over in which no runs are scored, so it exemplifies an over

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a man addressed as Sir has been made a knight

explanation.surface: A knight beheaded over a young woman, perhaps all of a sudden.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over of six balls with no runs conceded, so 'over maiden, maybe' gives OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Success that comes overnight arrives suddenly and unexpectedly fast, as if in a single night.

clue.text: English paper's showing creatures of land and water

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: An English newspaper is running a feature on amphibians.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S of "paper's" is read as the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Young newts are amphibians, animals that live both on land and in water.

clue.text: What may be distributed, e.g. for India?

definitions.text: What may be distributed, e.g. for India?

indicators.note: letters distributed are spread about and come out in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of help gets handed out to a country such as India.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is semi-&lit: 'distributed' shuffles E.G. FOR INDIA, while the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas development assistance is money and goods handed out by richer nations to countries like India.

clue.text: Understand the true nature of support to the bitter end?

definitions.meaning: to perceive what lies behind a pretence
to back a project or person until it is finished

explanation.surface: Grasping what something really is by standing by it to the last.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to detect a deception and to persist with a task until its completion.

clue.text: Thought opposing team "very hot"

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a side is a sports team
red hot, so red stands for very hot

explanation.surface: A rival team is reckoned to be in blistering form.
explanation.definitionFit: A considered view is one that has been thought about carefully, a past participle synonym.

clue.text: Independent worker restricted by money paid

indicators.note: something restricted by a sum is hemmed in by it, so the letter sits inside

parts.note: a fee is money paid for a service
the clue uses only the final letter of worker, with no word signalling the cut; the blog parses it the same way

explanation.surface: A freelancer is limited by what clients pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Nothing in the clue marks that only the end of 'worker' is wanted, so this is a loose clue; solvers fill it from the definition and crossers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not bound to or controlled by anyone else is independent, unrestrained.

clue.text: Pre-cooked food in can — hotel menu being awful!

indicators.note: a menu being awful suggests something wrong with it, so the letters get jumbled

explanation.surface: A grumble about tinned food and a hotel's dreadful menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'Pre-cooked food in can' shares 'can' with the fodder: CAN HOTEL MENU is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam and similar processed pork is sold cooked and ready-to-eat in tins.

clue.text: Football team run by he-man struggling to keep in charge

indicators.note: to keep means to hold the other letters within
a he-man struggling writhes about, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A football club managed by a muscle-man who is struggling to stay in control.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading German football club, based in Bavaria's capital, is one specific team.

clue.text: Light over small room making letters visible

parts.note: to light on something is to land or alight on it
the ladies is a women's lavatory, the smallest room in the house euphemistically

explanation.surface: A lamp above a small room helps to show up writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' wants to mean written characters; here it means people who let rooms. 'Light' is the verb, as in alight on, and the ladies is a British euphemism for a women's lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who let out rooms to lodgers are, in crossword wit, people who let.

clue.text: Most magnificent voice introducing story by saint

parts.note: to voice something is to state it
a story is a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: A grand voice opens a tale about a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of stately, describing the most dignified and impressive, matches most magnificent.

clue.text: Accusing, in the past, small boy, I don't let go

parts.note: Art is a short form of Arthur, a boy's name
to cling is to hold tight and not let go

explanation.surface: A little boy holding on and refusing to release something.
explanation.walkthrough: To article someone was, in older usage, to bring formal charges against them.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic verb meant to charge someone formally with specific counts, so its participle means accusing.

clue.text: After trendy numbers the writer's becoming serious

indicators.note: after means the next piece comes later in the answer than the earlier ones

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
tens are numbers
the writer's means I have, contracted to I've

explanation.surface: An author grows serious after a run of fashionable figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive work is concentrated and thorough, hence serious in its intensity.

clue.text: Worker in firm producing lyrical lines

indicators.note: the worker is placed in the firm, so its letters go inside

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
an ant is the classic crossword worker insect

explanation.surface: An employee at a company produces verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is a section of a long poem, a group of lyrical lines.

clue.text: Time short? Then there's little hesitation to provide bit of information

indicators.note: short means the word is cut and loses its final letter

parts.note: a date is a point in time
um is a small sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Short on time, someone stammers before giving a fact.
explanation.definitionFit: A single fact or item of data is a datum, the singular of data.

clue.text: Securing organic compound — container must be sound

indicators.note: the sound is the container, holding the compound inside it

parts.note: ting is the ringing sound of a bell or glass
ether is an organic compound

explanation.surface: Instructions for storing an organic chemical: the vessel has to be in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' first reads as 'in good condition', describing the container; it is really a noise, the ring of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Tying an animal or object down with a rope is securing it in place.

clue.text: Song rendered by lean lady, sung badly

indicators.note: something sung badly comes out mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tune performed poorly by a thin woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue text as held read 'lea lady', one N short; the blog's parse (LEAN LADY SUNG) restores it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots song by Burns is sung at New Year, a well-known example of a song.

clue.text: Plinth only having carbon at the centre

indicators.note: carbon at the centre puts that element in the middle of the other word

parts.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A pedestal made solely with carbon in its core.
explanation.definitionFit: A socle is an architectural base or plain pedestal, a synonym for a plinth.

clue.text: Something woodworker can hold: not rank?

definitions.meaning: a carpenter grips a rasp-like tool to smooth wood
in the phrase rank and ___, the ordinary soldiers stand apart from the rank

explanation.surface: A joiner's tool that is, oddly, not to be considered rank.
explanation.walkthrough: In a military formation, ranks are rows and the other lines are columns; the question mark flags the playful second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasp-like tool used by woodworkers, and the partner word to rank in the phrase for ordinary members.

clue.text: Bird making speed over the waves

definitions.meaning: a wading bird of the sandpiper family
nautical unit of speed, one nautical mile per hour

explanation.surface: A seabird zooming across the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a small wader and the nautical measure of speed are the same word.

clue.text: One horsey pair maybe but not a couple in partnership

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: but not means the next word's letter is taken away

parts.note: two horses harnessed together make a team

explanation.surface: A single horse, or perhaps two, but not a married couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people romantically linked are referred to as an item.

clue.text: Delicacy of record concerning first person in fashion

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
re means concerning, about

indicators.note: the first person sits in fashion, its letter placed inside

parts.note: ton means fashion or the fashionable set
I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: The tact shown in a record about someone fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicacy in the sense of tact and sensitivity is the same as discretion.

clue.text: Imbibers with urgent message "Time!" has interrupted?

indicators.note: the time letter has interrupted the message, breaking into it

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal, an urgent message

explanation.surface: Drinkers interrupted by the landlord's urgent call of last orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time!' is what a British pub landlord calls at closing.
explanation.definitionFit: Drunkards are habitual drinkers, people who imbibe heavily.

clue.text: Bad feeling about despatched soldiers, feature recurrent in battle

parts.note: re means about
sent means despatched
men are soldiers
the letter that appears twice in the word battle

explanation.surface: Bitterness over troops sent to fight again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter indignation at unfair treatment is bad feeling.
